quizzes.title: Refugees, Asylum Seekers and Migrants
quizzes.passage: The booklet separates three groups of people on the move: refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. Each group differs in the reason for moving, the protection it can receive and the law that governs its stay. A refugee is a person who is forced to flee because of persecution or conflict, and refugee status is recognised under an international framework that sets guidelines for host countries. An asylum seeker is a person who seeks recognition as a refugee, so a formal decision on the claim is still to come. A migrant, by contrast, moves mainly for work, education or better opportunities rather than to escape danger. The booklet also refers to several other international instruments that concern people on the move, including one that protects children and one based on the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. The categories also appear in the booklet's coverage of the Ceuta Migration Crisis, in which nearly 60000 migrants attempted to enter the Spanish enclave from Morocco in July 2026. Refugees, asylum seekers and migrants are all people on the move, but the booklet treats each category as distinct in law. The three terms are presented in a simple layout, with a short list of features under each heading.

questions.q: According to the booklet, which principle prohibits the forcible return of refugees?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that refugees cannot be forcibly returned, a principle it names non-refoulement.

questions.q: Which category of people does the booklet say does not qualify for refugee status?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the refugee framework specifies certain categories, such as war criminals, who do not qualify for refugee status.

questions.q: Who receives temporary protection during the application process, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says an asylum seeker receives temporary protection while the application is pending.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Migrants' stay is governed mainly by the domestic immigration laws of the country they enter.
Reason (R): Migrants may migrate legally or irregularly.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but whether a migration is legal or irregular does not explain which law governs the stay.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. 1967 Protocol   ->   A. Removed geographic and time limits on refugee protection
II. Global Compact on Refugees   ->   B. Framework to support refugees and host countries
III. Convention on the Rights of the Child   ->   C. Advocates for refugee children's welfare
IV. Article 14 of the UDHR   ->   D. Affirms the right to seek asylum from persecution
questions.explanation: The 1967 Protocol removed geographic and time limits, the Global Compact offers a support framework, the Convention on the Rights of the Child advocates for refugee children and Article 14 of the UDHR affirms the right to seek asylum.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Refugees are protected under the 1951 Refugee Convention.
II. Asylum seekers are governed mainly by domestic immigration laws.
III. Refugees can be forcibly returned if their home state requests it.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since domestic immigration laws govern migrants and refugees cannot be forcibly returned.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Asylum seekers are awaiting a decision on their refugee status.
II. Migrants are protected under the 1951 Refugee Convention.
III. Migrants move mainly to escape persecution.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the booklet describes migrants as moving for work, education or better opportunities.

quizzes.title: Refugee Law Terms and Instruments
quizzes.passage: The booklet separates three groups of people on the move: refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. Each group differs in the reason for moving, the protection it can receive and the law that governs its stay. A refugee is a person who is forced to flee because of persecution or conflict. The Refugee Convention is described as a comprehensive attempt to define refugees, and it sets guidelines for host countries to protect refugees and preserve their rights. An asylum seeker is a person who seeks recognition as a refugee. A migrant moves mainly for work, education or better opportunities rather than to escape danger. The booklet also refers to other international instruments that concern people on the move, including a framework that builds on a human rights declaration. The three categories also appear in the booklet's coverage of the Ceuta Migration Crisis, in which nearly 60000 migrants attempted to enter the Spanish enclave from Morocco in July 2026. Ceuta lies on the northern coast of Africa and borders Morocco. Refugees, asylum seekers and migrants are all people on the move, but the booklet treats each category as distinct in law. The booklet presents the three terms in a simple layout, with a short list of features under each heading.

questions.q: In which year was the Refugee Convention adopted, the instrument the booklet calls a comprehensive attempt to define refugees? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Refugee Convention to 1951.

questions.q: What term does the booklet give to the principle that refugees cannot be forcibly returned? (term)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the protection against forcible return non-refoulement.

questions.q: Which Article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights affirms the right to seek asylum from persecution? (article number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Global Compact on Refugees builds on Article 14 of the UDHR.

questions.q: Which category of people does the booklet say does not qualify for refugee status? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that war criminals do not qualify for refugee status.

questions.q: What is the name of the instrument that removed geographic and time limits on refugee protection? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 1967 Protocol expanded refugee protection beyond Europe by removing geographic and time limits.

questions.q: Which convention advocates for refugee children's welfare? (name)
questions.answer: Convention on the Rights of the Child
accept: Convention on Rights of the Child
UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Convention on the Rights of the Child advocates for refugee children's welfare.

questions.q: According to the booklet, migrants may migrate legally or what? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says migrants may migrate legally or irregularly.

quizzes.title: Spanish Territories and the Regional Dispute
quizzes.passage: Ceuta and Melilla are the best-known Spanish territories on the North African mainland, but the booklet places them within a larger group of Spanish holdings in the region. Spain exercises sovereignty over these territories, which the booklet describes as exclaves. Ceuta lies on the northern coast of Africa, on the Mediterranean Sea. Its neighbour is Morocco, and the booklet reports that nearly 60000 migrants attempted to enter the enclave from that country in July 2026. The booklet also places Ceuta within a wider regional picture that includes Western Sahara. That territory, described as a former Spanish colony, has been the subject of competing proposals and claims for many years. Several governments and movements have taken positions on its future, and the booklet records some of them. Ceuta is also described in the booklet as one of the shortest routes into European territory from Africa. Melilla, too, is one of the Spanish territories that the booklet names.

questions.q: Which group has demanded self-determination for the Sahrawi people?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Polisario Front demands self-determination for the Sahrawi people.

questions.q: Which country disputes the status of Ceuta, Melilla and the Plazas de Soberania?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Morocco disputes the status of these territories and has sought their return.

questions.q: Which issue does the booklet closely link to the Western Sahara dispute?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the migration issue is closely linked to the Western Sahara dispute.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Migration flows through Ceuta have been influenced by changes in Spain's relations with Morocco and Algeria.
Reason (R): Spain's relations with Morocco and Algeria have repeatedly changed over time.
Choose the correct option.
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: The booklet says changes in these relations have repeatedly influenced migration flows, so the reason explains the assertion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Polisario Front   ->   A. Declared the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic in 1976
II. Western Sahara   ->   B. Former Spanish colony annexed by Morocco in 1975
III. Algeria   ->   C. Supports the Polisario Front
IV. Morocco   ->   D. Proposes autonomy under its sovereignty
questions.explanation: The booklet links the Polisario Front to the 1976 declaration, Western Sahara to the 1975 annexation, Algeria to support for the Polisario and Morocco to its autonomy proposal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Algeria proposes autonomy under its sovereignty for Western Sahara.
II. Melilla is located on the Atlantic coast of Europe.
III. The Polisario Front demands self-determination for the Sahrawi people.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement III matches the booklet, since Morocco proposes autonomy and Melilla is a Spanish territory on the North African mainland.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Western Sahara was annexed by Morocco in 1975.
II. The Polisario Front declared the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic in 1975.
III. Algeria proposes autonomy under its sovereignty for Western Sahara.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the Polisario Front declared the SADR in 1976 and Algeria supports rather than proposes autonomy.

quizzes.title: Dates and Names in the Western Sahara Context
quizzes.passage: Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish territories on the North African mainland, and the booklet notes that they are not the only Spanish holdings in the region. Spain exercises sovereignty over these territories, which are described as exclaves. Morocco, the neighbouring country, has a long-standing position on their status that the booklet records. Ceuta lies on the northern coast of Africa, on the Mediterranean Sea, and sits close to Spain's European territory across a narrow strait. Western Sahara is a separate territory in the same region, and the booklet describes it as a former Spanish colony. Several parties have offered different proposals for its future. The booklet connects the migration issue at Ceuta with this wider dispute. It also says that Spain's relations with its neighbours have affected the flow of people through Ceuta over time. The booklet reports that nearly 60000 migrants attempted to enter Ceuta from Morocco in July 2026, and it places that event within this regional picture.

questions.q: In which year did Morocco gain independence, the year from which it has sought the return of these territories? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Morocco has sought their return since gaining independence in 1956.

questions.q: In which year was Western Sahara annexed by Morocco? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony, was annexed by Morocco in 1975.

questions.q: In which year did the Polisario Front declare the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Polisario Front declared the SADR in 1976.

questions.q: What is the name of the group of Spanish territories on the North African mainland that includes Ceuta and Melilla? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Ceuta, Melilla and Plazas de Soberania as the Spanish territories associated with the North African mainland.

questions.q: Which country supports the Polisario Front? (country)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Algeria supports the Polisario Front.

questions.q: What arrangement does Morocco propose for Western Sahara under its own sovereignty? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Morocco proposes autonomy under its sovereignty for Western Sahara.

questions.q: Which movement demands self-determination for the Sahrawi people? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Polisario Front demands self-determination for the Sahrawi people.

quizzes.title: UNHCR, Its Origins and Indian Law
quizzes.passage: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, known as UNHCR, is the UN body that works for refugees. It was formed in December 1950 as a successor to an earlier organisation that was set up after the Second World War. The idea behind the post is older. An office for refugees began under the League of Nations after the First World War, and its early work was led by a Norwegian explorer. The UNHCR's stated aim is to protect the rights of people fleeing conflict and persecution and to ensure a better future for them. The organisation has received the Nobel Peace Prize twice. The booklet also notes that World Refugee Day falls on June 20 and that its 2026 theme is Until Everyone Is Safe. The booklet also refers to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which safeguards individuals from torture or inhuman treatment upon return. In India, the booklet explains that undocumented foreigners are regulated under several older statutes.

questions.q: Which award honours exceptional service to refugees, displaced or stateless people each year?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the UNHCR Nansen Refugee Award as an annual honour for exceptional service to refugees, displaced or stateless people.

questions.q: Where are the headquarters of UNHCR located?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the UNHCR headquarters as Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: Which organisation did UNHCR succeed?
questions.explanation: The booklet says UNHCR was established in 1950 as successor to the International Refugee Organization (1946).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Passport (Entry into India) Act is one of the Acts that regulate undocumented foreigners in India.
Reason (R): The Citizenship Act was enacted in 1955.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the year of the Citizenship Act does not explain which Acts regulate undocumented foreigners.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Fridtjof Nansen   ->   A. Led the refugee office that originated under the League of Nations in 1921
II. UNHCR   ->   B. Formed on 14 December 1950
III. Registration of Foreigners Act   ->   C. Enacted in 1939
IV. Passport (Entry into India) Act   ->   D. Enacted in 1920
questions.explanation: Nansen led the League of Nations refugee office from 1921, UNHCR was formed in 1950, the Registration of Foreigners Act dates from 1939 and the Passport Act from 1920.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Nansen Refugee Award is presented by the League of Nations.
II. UNHCR has received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981.
III. UNHCR has received the Indira Gandhi Prize in 2015.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the Nansen Award is awarded by UNHCR, while statements II and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Nansen Refugee Award honours exceptional service to refugees, displaced or stateless people.
II. The Registration of Foreigners Act was enacted in 1955.
III. The Citizenship Act was enacted in 1955.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the Registration of Foreigners Act dates from 1939.

quizzes.title: UNHCR Dates and Indian Statutes
quizzes.passage: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, known as UNHCR, is the UN body that works to protect refugees and displaced people. It was formed as a successor to an earlier organisation set up after the Second World War. Its roots are older, since an office for refugees began under the League of Nations after the First World War, under the leadership of a Norwegian explorer. The UNHCR's headquarters are in a Swiss city, and its stated aim is to protect the rights of people fleeing conflict and persecution and to secure a better future for them. The organisation has received the Nobel Peace Prize twice. It also presents an annual award for exceptional service to refugees, displaced or stateless people. In India, undocumented foreigners are regulated under several Acts, which include laws on foreigners, passports and citizenship. The booklet also refers to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which safeguards individuals from torture or inhuman treatment upon return. World Refugee Day falls on June 20, and its 2026 theme is Until Everyone Is Safe.

questions.q: In which year did the office of the High Commissioner for Refugees originate under the League of Nations? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the office originated in 1921 under the League of Nations.

questions.q: In which year was UNHCR formed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives UNHCR's formation date as 14 December 1950.

questions.q: Which Act regulating undocumented foreigners in India was enacted in 1939? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Registration of Foreigners Act, 1939 among the Acts regulating undocumented foreigners.

questions.q: In which year did UNHCR first receive the Nobel Peace Prize? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says UNHCR received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1954 and 1981.

questions.q: Who led the League of Nations office for refugees whose origins UNHCR traces? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the office originated in 1921 under the League of Nations, led by Fridtjof Nansen.

questions.q: In which city are UNHCR's headquarters located? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists UNHCR's headquarters as Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Citizenship Act, 1955 among the Acts regulating undocumented foreigners.
